questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The car was being washed by me.

options.text: I had been washing the car.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'I was washing the car'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The structure of the active form of **'Past Continuous Tense'** is: **Subject+was\were+V+ing+Object.**

 
 
• **E.g.__​**- Ram was eating a mango. (Active Form)

 __
 
• A mango was being eaten by Ram. (Passive Form)
 
 
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is 'I was washing the car'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When the verb of a sentence is in the active voice, the subject is doing the acting, as in the sentence **“Kevin hit the ball.”**

 
 
• **Kevin** (the subject of the sentence) acts in relation to the ball.
 
 
 
• A verb is in the passive voice when the subject of the sentence is acted on by the verb.
 
 
• For example, in **“The ball was thrown by the pitcher,”** the ball (the subject) receives the action of the verb,
 
 

 and was thrown is in the passive voice.

 
• The same sentence cast in the active voice would be, **“The pitcher threw the ball.”**

questions.question:

Whenever he is / on a holiday, / he travels by foot / to the temple nearby.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'he travels by foot'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 
**'On foot'** is the more commonly used expression. It originates from the fact that 'on' is usually used for actions involving body parts.

 
 
• 
 
**E.g.**__- He went to the temple __on foot__.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**'By'** is usually used to talk about a means of transport (i.e. train, car, boat, plane, etc).

 __
 
• 
 
He goes to the office by train__.

 
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is: *Whenever he is on a holiday, he travels **on **foot to the temple nearby.*

__
 
• The given sentence is in the form of **'Past Perfect Tense+would have+v3'. **
 
• It belongs to the **'Third Conditional Sentence'.**** **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

• There are always two parts to a conditional sentence – one part beginning with 'if' to describe a possible situation and the second part which describes the consequence.
 
 
• **For example**__: If it rains, we'll get wet.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

All the electric poles in the suburbs were destroyed by the cyclone last year.

options.text: The cyclone destroyed all the electric poles in the suburbs last year.
The cyclone was being destroyed with all the electric poles in the suburbs last year.
The cyclone was destroyed by the all the electric poles in the suburbs last year.
The cyclone destroyed all the suburbs by the electric poles last year

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'The cyclone destroyed all the electric poles in the suburbs last year'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **Passive Voice**. As per the question we have to change it into** Active Voice.**
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• **​Subject + V² + Object. (Active Voice)**
 
• **Subject(objective case) + was/were +V³ + Object(subjective case). (Passive Voice)**
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• Their cousin showed them some rare photographs.** (Active Voice)**
 
• They were shown some rare photographs by their cousin.** (Passive Voice)**
 
 
 
• **​The subject **of the given sentence is **'All the electric poles'.**
 
• **The object** of the given sentence is **'the cyclone'.**
 
• **The subject **will be put in place of **the object **and **the object** will be put in place of **the subject.**
 
• And **'were destroyed' **will be changed into** 'destroyed'.**

**​Correct sentence:__ ***The cyclone destroyed all the electric poles in the suburbs last year.*

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. The deeper you immerse it, the greater will be the difference in the water level.

B. This difference in the levels in the U-tube is a measure of the pressure applied by your palm.

C. If you immerse the funnel into a bucket of water, you will again see the difference in the water level in the U-tube.

D. When you gently apply pressure on the rubber film with your palm, you will find that a difference in the water level is created in the manometer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'DBCA'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• ** **While arranging the parts of the passage, **we should find some grammatical or contextual connections between them-**__

 
 
• **​D is the first sentence** as it describes the difference in the water level is created in the manometer.
 
• **B is the second sentence** as it describes the measures of the pressure of the water levels in the U - tube.
 
• **C is the third sentence** as it describes you will again see the difference in the water level if you immerse the funnel into a bucket of water.
 
• **A is the last sentence** as it concludes the deeper you immerse it, the greater will be the difference.
 
 

**Thus, the correct order is DBCA:**

 
• **d**. When you gently apply pressure on the rubber film with your palm, you will find that a difference in the water level is created in the manometer.
 
• **b. **This difference in the levels in the U-tube is a measure of the pressure applied by your palm.
 
• **c.** If you immerse the funnel into a bucket of water, you will again see the difference in the water level in the U-tube.
 
• **a.** The deeper you immerse it, the greater will be the difference in the water level.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The utensils have been cleaned.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The type of the sentence is passive voice.
 
• The tense of the given sentence is **Present Perfect.**
 
• In the given sentence, 'The utensils' act as the object in the active voice and as the subject in the passive voice form.
 
 
• **Passive Format: Subject + have/has been + past participle (V3) + (by + **agent).
 
• **Active Format: Subject + have/has + past participle (V3).**
 
 
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• Passive example: The letter has been mailed.
 
• Active example: Someone has mailed the letter.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is- ***"Someone has cleaned the utensils."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Option 1, "Someone is cleaning the utensils," suggests an action that is currently in progress (Present Continuous tense), which does not match the completeness implied by the Present Perfect tense in the original sentence.
 
• Option 2, "Someone was cleaning the utensils," implies a past continuous action, which is not compatible with the original sentence's Present Perfect tense, indicating an action that has been completed at some point in the past but is relevant in the present moment.
 
• Option 3, "Someone cleaned the utensils," uses Simple Past tense, indicating a completed action in the past with no direct implication of its relevance to the present moment, which differs from the Present Perfect tense's usage in the original sentence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **When changing from active to passive voice (or vice versa):**

 
 
• The tense of the sentence should not be changed.
 
• Only the structure is altered to shift focus between the doer and the receiver of the action.
